headline: High-risk default write/egress overlap: Kestra can act on Argo outputs, creating dangerous cascading errors and data leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and parameters, and Kestra reads files, stdin/stdout, and many external channels. That creates a plausible default bridge where content from agent_a can be consumed by agent_b as workflow input. No direct provenance or isolation mechanism is shown, so injected instructions in artifacts are a realistic risk.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts or parameters are copied into agent_b workflow inputs
IF agent_b parses file or stdout content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Kestra consumes Argo outputs
Prefix all transferred content as data, not instructions
Use separate storage paths for handoff files
Enable content provenance tags in the orchestrator chain
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all cross-agent payloads

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches artifacts and parameters, while agent_b reads and writes filesystem data and has broad network egress plus many external integrations. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive artifacts can flow from Argo into Kestra and then out through logs, notifications, or cloud targets. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or storage bucket
IF agent_b forwards imported artifacts into logs, notifications, or external services
mitigations: Store handoff files in a separate restricted directory
Disable unnecessary outbound integrations in Kestra
Redact secrets from artifacts before transfer
Review logs for copied payloads after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a can call APIs and agent_b can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Kestra also supports multiple instances, so concurrent runs can race on shared mutable resources if both agents target the same files, jobs, or external endpoints. The overlap is dangerous by default because agent_b has broad write and execution power.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared external resource
IF Kestra instances run concurrently against the same workflow state
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent
Serialize runs that touch the same resource
Lock shared files before writes
Disable concurrent instances for shared workflows
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo produces workflow artifacts and parameters, and Kestra can consume files/stdin and trigger downstream actions like email, Slack, cloud, or SSH. That makes agent_b likely to treat agent_a output as authoritative unless an explicit verification step is added. Because Kestra can take real actions, a bad Argo output can cascade into irreversible operational mistakes.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Argo-produced artifacts or parameters as task inputs
IF downstream Kestra tasks send notifications or execute infrastructure actions
mitigations: Insert a validation task before any action-taking step
Require human approval for destructive workflows
Compare Argo outputs against expected schemas
Log and diff inputs before execution
requires-engineering: add signed outputs from agent_a

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents touch artifacts and workflow data, but agent_b additionally handles logs, messages, notifications, and cloud data, which broadens retention and residency exposure. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a proven breach. Uncertainty pushes this above low because the default surface area is large.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra notifications, logs, or cloud integrations
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through Kestra
Disable logging of sensitive payloads
Set short retention on workflow logs
Restrict notifications for regulated workflows
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
